To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the UN has not been responsive to oppositional voices and has not changed the development paradigm in the transition from Millennium Development Goals to Sustainable Development Goals.

the UN has not been responsive to the criticisms articulated by liberal feminists and World Forum Social Forum critics, and has not incorporated the values, representations, and problem solution frames articulated by these oppositional voices.
the UN has been responsive to oppositional voices in the construction of the Sustainable Development goals, but that the influence of neoliberalism is still evident.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how and to what extent the Sustainable Development Goals reflect the voices and concerns of the poor and marginalised.

how the UN's development agenda has changed over the past 15 years and the extent to which it has been influenced by the dominant economic discourse, neoliberalism, and the extent to the which it has been responsive to oppositional voices.

how the United Nations has responded to the critiques of the Millennium Development Goal and the extent to which the Sustainable Development Goals have addressed the issues that were identified by the Millennium Development Goals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the United Nations is not responsive to oppositional voices, as the Sustainable Development Goals remain largely the same in terms of the economic paradigm, but have been rebranded to be more inclusive of the environment and social development.
the UN has failed to address the issues raised by the oppositional voices, and has instead continued to perpetuate the dominant economic discursive framework.
there is no significant change in the economic discourses of the Millennium Development and Sustainable Development Goals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the United Nations is a global organisation with the responsibility to protect the rights of people, but the Sustainable Development Goals do not address the fundamental problems of poverty and inequality.
the Millennium Development Goals were constructed within a neoliberal economic paradigm, which failed to address the structural causes of poverty.
the Sustainable Development Goals have not addressed the concerns of critics of the Millennium Development Goal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
while there is a shift in the Sustainable Development Goals away from neoliberalism, it is not a wholesale rejection.
the United Nations' response to criticisms of the Millennium Development goals was to incorporate them into the Sustainable Development goals.

while the UN has made some progress in responding to critiques of the Millennium Development Goal, the Sustainable Development Goal remains dominated by neoliberal economic discourses and is therefore unlikely to achieve the desired outcomes.
